planting.note: Plant after frost danger passes; mulch roots over winter in zone 7.

directions: Set out in rich, well-drained soil where arching stems have room to spread. Pale yellow tubular flowers dangle in loose panicles from early summer into fall, drawing hummingbirds. Cut dieback stems to the base in late winter since top growth is often damaged by cold even where roots survive. Deadhead spent flower spikes to extend the bloom season.

planting.note: Plant after frost danger passes; protect crown with mulch in colder zones.

directions: Grow in sun with consistently moist, well-drained soil for the densest flowering display. Glossy foliage sets off abundant orange-red, yellow-throated tubular blooms from early summer until hard frost. Prune hard in spring to remove winter-damaged wood and encourage fresh basal shoots. Deadhead through the season to keep new flower spikes coming.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; transplant once nights stay above 50F.

directions: Site in full sun with evenly moist, fertile soil for the heaviest flush of blooms. Rounded clusters of deep purple flowers carry a strong vanilla fragrance all summer, making this a favorite for pots near seating areas. Pinch growing tips early to build a bushier plant with more flowering stems. Bring a cutting indoors before frost to overwinter as a houseplant.

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained, low-phosphorus soil.

directions: Plant in sharply draining, low-fertility soil and avoid phosphorus-rich fertilizers that harm Proteaceae roots. Needle-like foliage backs waxy rose-red spider flowers produced from late autumn through spring, drawing nectar birds. Use as an informal hedge or screen, trimming lightly after flowering to maintain density. Established plants tolerate drought, wind, and light frost once roots are settled.

planting.note: Plant in spring into sharply drained, low-phosphorus soil.

directions: Grow in full sun with excellent drainage and minimal fertilizer, since this Proteaceae hybrid resents phosphorus and wet feet. Bracts shift seasonally through pink, cream, and burgundy tones, intensifying in cooler weather for long-lasting color without any flowers needed. Keep an upright, bushy form with an occasional tip prune after the color display fades. Use as a waterwise accent or cut-foliage subject in coastal and dry gardens.

planting.note: Divide or plant corms in spring; avoid disturbing established clumps.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained soil where wiry arching stems can sway freely without crowding neighbors. Deep red-purple, bell-shaped flowers dangle from fine wands held above grassy evergreen foliage, among the darkest of all dierama selections. Leave clumps undisturbed for several years, since this genus resents root disturbance and transplants poorly. Cut faded flower wands back after bloom but retain foliage through winter for crown protection.

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained, low-phosphorus soil; tolerates coastal salt spray.

directions: Plant in full sun with sharp drainage, since this dwarf conebush resists root rot far better than most banksias once established. Golden-yellow flower spikes with contrasting reddish styles glow along the branch tips from early autumn through winter. The dense, mounding form suits rockeries, low borders, or mass coastal plantings without any pruning needed. Water sparingly after establishment, as the plant is highly drought and salt-wind tolerant.
sources: Royal Botanic Garden Sydney horticultural notes

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained soil; shelter from harsh winter wind in colder zones.

directions: Plant in full sun to light shade in well-drained soil, where this compact hybrid stays noticeably smaller and rounder than other Mexican orange cultivars. Fragrant white star-shaped flowers open in spring and often repeat in late summer against glossy dark green leaves. Little pruning is needed beyond removing stray shoots to keep the mounded shape tidy. Established plants shrug off short dry spells and need minimal winter protection within their hardiness range.
